phonics.title: The Bus
phonics.text: Ben and Nan got on a bus. Ben had a nap. Nan did not nap. Nan had to get Ben up to get off.

questions.question: Who got on the bus with Ben?
Who had a nap?
Why did Nan not nap?
questions.answer: She had to get Ben up to get off the bus.

phonics.reason: Removed clock time 'At ten' and American 'cab'; title said Van but phase 2 cannot spell van, so now a bus; Mum driving removed.

phonics.title: Bob in Bed
phonics.text: Bob is in bed. The sun is up. Dad ran in. Dad got Bob up. Bob is not mad. Bob had a hug.

questions.question: Who is in bed?
What did Bob have?
Why did Dad get Bob up?
questions.answer: The sun was up / it was time to get up.

phonics.reason: Clock time 'It is ten' replaced by 'The sun is up'; when-question swapped for a what-question.

phonics.title: Zeb the Cat
phonics.text: Zeb is a cat. Zeb sat in the bin and had a nap. Jen shut the lid. Zeb is in the bin! Zeb is sad.

questions.question: Where did Zeb have a nap?
What did Jen shut?
Why is Zeb sad?
questions.answer: He is shut in the bin.

phonics.reason: 'check the bin' is an idiom; now 'look in the bin'.

phonics.title: The Shop
phonics.text: Fran went to the shop to get milk. The shop was shut. A man said, "Back soon." Fran sat on a step and waited.

questions.question: What did Fran go to get?
Where did Fran sit?
Why did Fran wait?

phonics.reason: Removed 'shut till ten' clock time and adult word 'clerk'.

phonics.title: The Bus
phonics.text: Josh and Nan went on a bus. The bus had men and kids on it. Nan sat down. A man got up and let Josh sit. Josh said thanks.

questions.question: Who was on the bus with Josh and Nan?
Who let Josh sit?
Why did the man get up?
questions.answer: So Josh could sit (Josh had no seat).

phonics.reason: 'packed' and 'a spot' are ambiguous; now the bus has men and kids on it and Nan sat down.

phonics.title: The Crab
phonics.text: Pam and Jim went to a rock pool. They had a look at a crab. Jim bent down to pat it. The crab pinched his hand! Jim yelped and jumped back.

questions.question: Where did Pam and Jim go?
What did they look at?
Why did Jim yelp?

phonics.reason: 'spotted' (could mean dotted) replaced with 'had a look at'.

phonics.title: The Flag
phonics.text: Stan and Jess got a flag at the shop. They ran up the hill with it and stuck it in a crack. A strong wind hit the flag and it fell down.

questions.question: What did Stan and Jess get at the shop?
Where did they stick the flag?
questions.answer: In a crack on the hill.

questions.question: Why did the flag fall down?

phonics.title: The Dentist
phonics.text: Sam had a bad tooth. He went to the dentist. She looked at it and got Sam a red toothbrush. Sam was sad, but he will brush his teeth with the toothbrush a lot.

questions.question: Who did Sam go to see?
What did the dentist get Sam?
Why did Sam go to the dentist?

phonics.reason: 'checked', 'upset', 'from now on' replaced with plain words.

phonics.title: The Elf
phonics.text: An elf lost his hat. He looked in the shed, in the dustbin and under his blanket. The elf was sad. Then he felt a bump in his bag. The hat was in the bag!

questions.question: What did the elf lose?
Where was the hat?
Why was the elf sad?

phonics.title: The Rocket
phonics.text: Josh and Jess had a rocket at the picnic. They painted it red and stuck a flag on top. It was not big, but Gran said it was the best rocket at the picnic. Josh and Jess had big smiles.

questions.question: What did Josh and Jess have at the picnic?
What did they stick on top?
Why did Josh and Jess have big smiles?
questions.answer: Gran said it was the best rocket.

phonics.reason: Removed 'contest' and 'boss'; simple family praise instead.

phonics.title: The Hamster
phonics.text: Nan's hamster got out. It isn't in its box. Nan looked in the basket and in her jacket. Then she felt a bump in her pocket. It was the hamster!

questions.question: Whose hamster got out?
Where did Nan find the hamster?
Why did Nan look in the basket and in her jacket?
questions.answer: She was looking for the hamster / it had got out.

phonics.title: The Market
phonics.text: Dad took Josh to the market. Josh had the basket. Dad got a pumpkin and some mushrooms and dropped them in it. Soon the basket had lots in it, and Josh's arms started to hurt. “It's my turn to have it,” said Dad.

questions.question: Who had the basket at first?
What did Dad get at the market?
Why did Dad say it was his turn to have the basket?
questions.answer: It had lots in it and Josh's arms hurt.

phonics.title: The Lost Boy
phonics.text: Roy was at the fair. He looked round but Dad was not there. Roy called out. A helper found him and took him to a tent. Dad was in the tent!

questions.question: Where was Roy?
Who found Roy?
Why did Roy call out?
questions.answer: He could not see Dad / he was lost.

phonics.reason: Adult word 'clerk' and shop replaced with a helper and a tent.

phonics.title: The Lake
phonics.text: It was a hot day. Luke and Kate ran to the lake. Kate jumped in. Luke stayed on the sand. He had left his swim kit at home.

questions.question: When did Luke and Kate run to the lake?
Where did Luke and Kate run?
Why did Luke stay on the sand?
questions.answer: He had left his swim kit at home.

phonics.reason: Removed date 'in June' and confusing 'bank' (now sand).

report: 14 of 60 texts changed, all pass check_text and mix_problems. Patterns: clock times/dates 4 (1-2 'At ten', 1-4 'It is ten', 5-1 'shut till ten', 8-4 'in June'); Americanism 1 (cab, 1-2, now a bus because van cannot be spelled at phase 2 and Mum-driving removed); adult words 3 (clerk in 5-1 and 7-2, contest/boss in 6-3); idioms/ambiguous words 9 (checked in 2-4, 6-0, 6-1, 6-4; packed in 5-2, 6-5; spotted 5-3; gust 5-4; upset and 'from now on' in 6-0; 'bank' in 8-4). Two when-questions with clock answers were swapped to who/what (1-2, 1-4); 8-4 keeps a when question answered 'On a hot day'. Redraw: 1-2 (bus, Nan), 1-4 (sun up), 5-1 (no clerk), 6-3 (no contest, Gran, picnic), 7-2 (helper, tent), 8-4 (sand). Left alone: 'mad' meaning cross in 1-1 and 1-4 (standard UK phonics usage, no decodable phase-2 alternative that reads better), 'On Monday' (9-3), 'till home time' (10-3), dentist, basket, garden, hamster, market, match, gym, barber, muffins and the rest, which are within a 5-7 year old's experience.
